text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended a low-action day slightly firmer with the cash market up around 40 basis points and the June future on the Milan futures market notching up gains of more than 30 basis points.

With LIFFE closed for a one-day public holiday however the market was fairly thin. The February 2007 cash Btp ended 43 basis points up at 95.70 with a yield of 7.5 percent and a spread over the benchmark German Bund of 174 basis points.
The June BTP future on MIF was 34 basis points higher at 128.18 and the lira was cruising around 988.40/8.70 per mark, little changed on early morning levels.

The Italian government announced it was calling a confidence vote to shove the controversial mini-budget through parliament. The vote in the lower house will be this government's 20th confidence vote since it took office a year ago.
The mini-budget for 15.5 trillion lire of budget deficit cutting measures is designed to whip Italy's deficit into shape to meet the tough Maastricht criteria on European monetary union.
Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the budget deficit for the first half of 1997 would be less than half the 52.25 trillion lire seen in the 1996 first half.
Tuesday sees the release of Italy's final consumer prices data for April, with 1.7 percent expected after March's rate of 2.2 percent year on year.
